from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A matrix acts as a transformation function.", "Vectors change position through these functions.", "We visualize grid distortions by matrices."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Linear Transformation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Objects
        vec_v = Vector([1, 1], color="#ADD8E6")
        label_v = MathTex("v", color="#ADD8E6")
        matrix_a = MathTex("A", color="#FFD700")
        vec_v_prime = Vector([2, 0], color="#FF6347")
        label_v_prime = MathTex("v'", color="#FF6347")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.place_at_grid(vec_v, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, "B3")
        self.play(Create(vec_v), Write(label_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF6347")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "D2")
        self.play(Write(matrix_a))
        
        # Transform vector
        self.play(
            vec_v.animate.become(vec_v_prime),
            label_v.animate.move_to(self.grid["D4"]),
            FadeIn(label_v_prime.move_to(self.grid["D5"]))
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Visualizing grid distortion
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.play(grid.animate.apply_matrix([[1, 1], [0, 1]])) # Shear transform
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Composition", [
            "Sequence two transformations for complex results.",
            "Apply transformation B then apply A.",
            "The combined effect creates composition."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Introduce function f (blue #4169E1) and g (green #32CD32)
        f_label = MathTex("f", color="#4169E1")
        g_label = MathTex("g", color="#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(f_label, "B2", scale_factor=2)
        self.place_at_grid(g_label, "B5", scale_factor=2)
        self.play(Write(f_label), Write(g_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold for active

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show the composition g(f(v)) as a chained process
        v_label = MathTex("v")
        comp = MathTex("g(f(v))")
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, "D2", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(comp, "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(v_label), Write(comp))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the combined mapping as a single operation
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(comp, color=WHITE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Composition is written as A(Bv).", "This equals the matrix product AB.", "AB captures the combined transformation instruction."]
        self.setup_layout("Deriving the Matrix Product", lecture_lines)
        
        matrix_a = Matrix([[ "a_{11}", "a_{12}" ], [ "a_{21}", "a_{22}" ]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.8).scale(0.5)
        matrix_b = Matrix([[ "b_{11}", "b_{12}" ], [ "b_{21}", "b_{22}" ]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.8).scale(0.5)
        matrix_ab = Matrix([[ "c_{11}", "c_{12}" ], [ "c_{21}", "c_{22}" ]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.8).scale(0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_b, "B4", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a), FadeIn(matrix_b))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_ab, "E3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_ab))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Highlight columns
        matrix_ab.get_columns()[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        matrix_ab.get_columns()[1].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.play(Indicate(matrix_ab))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Non-Commutativity", [
            "Order of operations matters significantly.", 
            "Apply A then B differs.", 
            "Applying B then A yields another."
        ])
        
        # Objects to animate
        square_a = Square(side_length=1, color="#D3D3D3", fill_opacity=0.5)
        square_b = Square(side_length=1, color="#A9A9A9", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(square_a, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(square_b, 'C5')
        self.add(square_a, square_b)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFE0")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFDAB9")
        # Apply A then B: A=Rotate(90), B=Shift(right)
        self.play(
            Rotate(square_a, angle=PI/2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            square_a.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#E0FFFF")
        # Applying B then A: B=Shift(right), A=Rotate(90)
        self.play(
            square_b.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Rotate(square_b, angle=PI/2),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrix multiplication is functional composition.",
            "It powers modern graphics and robotics.",
            "Transformations are essential geometric tools."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        summary_icon = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(summary_icon, "B2")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_icon))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        robot_arm = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*1.5),
            Circle(radius=0.2).move_to(RIGHT*1.5)
        ).set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(robot_arm, "D4")
        self.play(Create(robot_arm))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Ending
        self.play(FadeOut(self.title), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(summary_icon), FadeOut(robot_arm))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Linear Transformation
sections.content: Define a matrix as a function that transforms a vector. Visually represent a 2D grid being stretched/rotated by a matrix 'A'. Explain that v' = Av.
sections.example: A 2D vector [1, 0] being rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise by matrix A.

sections.title: The Concept of Composition
sections.content: Introduce the idea of applying two transformations sequentially. If transformation A is applied after transformation B, the total effect is a single combined transformation C.
sections.example: A 'Robot Arm' sequence: First, a Rotation matrix (B) turns the arm, then a Scaling matrix (A) extends it.

sections.title: Deriving the Matrix Product
sections.content: Show that the composition (A ∘ B)v = A(Bv). Through substitution, demonstrate that the result is equivalent to (AB)v. Emphasize that the matrix product AB is simply the 'combined instruction manual' for the two transformations.
sections.example: Tracking a cat's movement: Matrix B rotates the cat's coordinate system, and Matrix A flips it; show how AB combines these into one single net-transformation matrix.

sections.title: Visualizing Non-Commutativity
sections.content: Use an animation to show that applying A then B is not the same as B then A. This explains why matrix multiplication AB ≠ BA.
sections.example: A character performing a 'Jump' (Transformation A) then a 'Spin' (Transformation B) results in a different final position than 'Spin' then 'Jump'.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Reiterate that matrix multiplication is not just arithmetic—it is the functional composition of geometric transformations. This provides the foundation for computer graphics and robotics.
sections.example: A 3D video game character: Matrix chains (Bone transformations) determine where the character's hand ends up in space.
